$comment: Shared numeric contract for the on-demand image endpoint, `/__ruvyxa/image`.
Two request hosts answer that path and neither can import the other's
constants:
- crates/ruvyxa_dev_server/src/dynamic_image.rs   (`dev`, `start`, `preview`)
- packages/ruvyxa/runtime/serverless-handler.mjs  (every deployed build,
through the optimizer an
adapter supplies)
They had disagreed about `defaultQuality`. The native host answers an absent
`q` with the project's own `image.quality`; the deployed handler answered it
with a hardcoded 82 and read no project value at all, because `ruvyxa build`
published `onDemand` and `maxWidth` into the runtime policy and not the
quality beside them. A project setting `image.quality: 60` therefore got 60
under `ruvyxa dev` and 82 from Vercel or Cloudflare for the same URL — two
different images from one configuration, and nothing about a re-encoded photo
fails a build or shows up in a log.
The width and quality bounds are here for the same reason even though they
agree today: they are the rest of what a caller can send, both hosts encode
them separately, and a bound that drifts turns a working URL into a 400 on
one deployment target only.
Every implementation replays this file:
- crates/ruvyxa_dev_server/src/dynamic_image.rs            (Rust host)
- tests/packages/ruvyxa/serverless-shared-tables.test.mjs  (deployed handler,
plus the two
sources that carry
the value to it)
Change a bound here first; a port that drifts then fails in the language that
drifted rather than on one deployment target after release.
